## Self-Reported Disability Status

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Self-assessed disability status
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
disability_status <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Disability_Status.csv")

# Data wrangling
disability_status <- disability_status %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(has_profound_core_activity_limitation_n:has_no_disability_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(profound_n     = has_profound_core_activity_limitation_n,
                severe_n       = has_severe_core_activity_limitation_n,
                moderate_n     = has_moderate_core_activity_limitation_n,
                mild_n         = has_mild_core_activity_limitation_n,
                restriction_n  = has_a_schooling_employment_restriction_only_n,
                nolimitation_n = has_no_limitation_or_specific_restriction_n,
                nodisability_n = has_no_disability_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(profound_n:nodisability_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("profound"),
                starts_with("severe"),
                starts_with("moderate"),
                starts_with("mild"),
                starts_with("restriction"),
                starts_with("nolimitation"),
                starts_with("nodisability"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "profound"     = "Profound limitation",
                                              "severe"       = "Severe limitation",
                                              "moderate"     = "Moderate limitation",
                                              "mild"         = "Mild limitation",
                                              "restriction"  = "Schooling or work restriction",
                                              "nolimitation" = "No limitation or restriction",
                                              "nodisability" = "No disability",
                                              "answered"     = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Profound limitation",
                                           "Severe limitation",
                                           "Moderate limitation",
                                           "Mild limitation",
                                           "Schooling or work restriction",
                                           "No limitation or restriction",
                                           "No disability",
                                           "Total")))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Type of disability
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
disability_type <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Disability_Type.csv")

# Data wrangling
disability_type <- disability_type %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = total_n - no_disability_n) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(sensory_n    = sensory_and_speech_n,
                learning_n   = learning_and_understanding_n,
                physical_n   = physical_restriction_n,
                headinjury_n = head_injury_stroke_or_acquired_brain_injury_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(sensory_n:other_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("sensory"),
                starts_with("learning"),
                starts_with("physical"),
                starts_with("psychosocial"),
                starts_with("headinjury"),
                starts_with("other"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "sensory"      = "Sensory or speech",
                                              "learning"     = "Learning or understanding",
                                              "physical"     = "Physical",
                                              "psychosocial" = "Psychosocial",
                                              "headinjury"   = "Head injury",
                                              "other"        = "Other",
                                              "answered"     = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Sensory or speech",
                                           "Learning or understanding",
                                           "Physical",
                                           "Psychosocial",
                                           "Head injury",
                                           "Other",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 28% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne reported that they were living with a disability that results in specific limitations with any core activities (mobility, communication and self-care). This equates to approximately 11,000 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people in Greater Melbourne.

- Males were more likely than females to be living with a disability that results in specific restriction when participating in schooling or work activities (20% vs. 2.8%).

- The most commonly reported disabilities by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne were physical restrictions (57% of survey respondents who were living with a disability, approximately 9,900 people), and sensory or speech issues (38% of survey respondents who were living with a disability, approximately 6,600 people).

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following questions were asked of all people completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey.

- Can you do any of the following activities? (Select all that apply)
  - Easily walk 200 metres
  - Walk up and down stairs without a handrail
  - Easily bend to pick up an object from the floor
  - Use public transport without difficulty, help, or supervision
  - None of the above

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>
  
- Do you have any of these conditions that have lasted, or are expected to last, for six months or longer? (Select all that apply)
  - Shortness of breath
  - Chronic or recurring pain
  - A nervous or emotional condition
  - Memory problems or periods of confusion
  - Social or behavioural difficulties
  - Long term effects as a result of a head injury, stroke, or other brain damage
  - Receiving treatment or medication for any other long term condition
  - Any other long term health condition (e.g. arthritis, asthma, heart disease)
  - None of the above

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- Do you have any of these conditions that have lasted, or are expected to last, for six months or longer? (Select all that apply)
  - Sight problems not corrected by glasses or contact lenses
  - Hearing problems
  - Speech problems
  - Blackouts, seizures, or loss of consciousness
  - Difficulty learning or understanding things
  - Limited use of arms or fingers
  - Difficulty gripping things
  - Limited use of legs or feet
  - Any condition that restricts physical activity pr physical work (e.g. back problems, migraines)
  - Any disfigurement or deformity
  - Any mental illness for which help or supervision is required
  - None of the above

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- If yes, are you restricted in your everyday activities because of this condition?
  - Yes
  - No
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- If yes, do you ever need help, supervision, or aids to help with any of these tasks because of this condition? (Select all that apply)
  - Bathing or showering
  - Dressing or undressing
  - Eating or feeding
  - Going to the toilet, bladder control, or bowel control
  - Moving around away from home or moving around at home
  - Getting in or out of a bed or chair
  - Understanding or being understood by strangers, friends, or family (including use of sign language or lip reading)
  - None of the above

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- If yes, do you have any of the following problems with schooling because of this condition? (Select all that apply)
  - Not attending school or further study
  - Needing time off from school or study
  - Attending special classes or school
  - Other related difficulties
  - No difficulty with education

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- If yes, do you have any of the following problems with work because of this condition? (Select all that apply)
  - Type of job you can do
  - Number of hours that can be worked
  - Finding suitable work
  - Needing time off work
  - Permanently unable to work
  - Other related difficulties
  - No difficulty with work

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

#### Figure 10B-1

::: {#fig_10B_1 .fig-tab-title}
**Figure 10B-1:** Self-reported disability status for survey respondents who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander, Greater Melbourne, by sex, 2022-2023
:::

```{r}
#
figure_count <- figure_count + 1

factor_levels <- stringr::str_wrap(levels(disability_status$answer), width = 17)

figure_number <- disability_status %>% 
  dplyr::filter(sex != "Total" & !answer %in% c("Total", "No disability")) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(stringr::str_wrap(answer, width = 17), levels = factor_levels)) %>%
  #
  f_bar_grouped_sex(x_variable = answer,
                    y_variable = n,
                    y_max      = NA,
                    y_breaks   = 500,
                    y_expand   = 300,
                    x_angle    = 90)

figure_percent <- disability_status %>% 
  dplyr::filter(sex != "Total" & !answer %in% c("Total", "No disability")) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(stringr::str_wrap(answer, width = 17), levels = factor_levels)) %>%
  #
  f_bar_grouped_sex(x_variable = answer,
                    y_variable = prop,
                    y_max      = 25,
                    y_breaks   = 5,
                    y_expand   = 0.5,
                    x_angle    = 90)

f_bar_grouped_combine(figure_number, figure_percent, legend_offset = -0.35)
```

- A person was defined as having a disability if they had an impairment which restricts their everyday activities and that has lasted, or is expected to last, for at least six months.

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- People with disabilities were classified by whether they had:
  - a specific limitation with any core activities (mobility, communication and self-care),
  - a specific restriction when participating in schooling or employment activities, or
  - no specific limitation with core activities or restriction with schooling or employment activities.

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- For Figure 10B-2 and Table 10B-2, *head injury* includes head injuries, strokes, and/or acquired brain injuries.

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>

## Assistance with Core Activities

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Assistance with core activities, by LGA
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
assist_lga <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Disability_Assistance_LGA.csv",
                                variable = "assist") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(assist != "Not stated")

# Data wrangling
assist_lga <- assist_lga %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(assist = dplyr::case_when(
    assist == "Has need for assistance with core activities" ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no")) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = assist,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "yes")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Assistance with core activities, by age and sex
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
assist_agesex <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_Disability_Assistance_AgeSex.csv",
                                      variable = "assist") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(assist != "Not stated")

# Data wrangling
assist_agesex <- assist_agesex %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(assist = dplyr::case_when(
    assist == "Has need for assistance with core activities" ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no")) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = assist,
                          dichot   = "yes")
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Overall, 9.4% (n = 1,116) of people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census required assistance with core activities (mobility, communication, and/or self-care). This was higher than for non-Indigenous people living in the NEPHU catchment (6.0%).

- The number of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who required assistance with core activities ranged from 211 (Hume LGA) to 20 (Nillumbik LGA).

- The gap between the observed number of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people who required assistance with core activities and the number expected if the rate was the same as for non-Indigenous people was biggest for Yarra Ranges and Hume LGAs.

- The percentage of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who required assistance with core activities ranged from 12% (Hume LGA) to 5.4% (Nillumbik LGA).

- The percentage of people living in the NEPHU catchment who required assistance with core activities increased with increasing age for both males and females.

- There was also a second peak in the number of people requiring assistance with core activities for both males and females aged 10-19 years.

- More Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people required assistance with core activities than expected based on the non-Indigenous population across most age groups and both genders. The gap was highest for males aged 10-19 years.

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following questions were asked of all people completing the ABS Census 2021.

- Does the person ever need someone to help with, or be with them for, self-care activities?
  - Yes, always
  - Yes, sometimes
  - No
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- Does the person ever need someone to help with, or be with them for, body movement activities?
  - Yes, always
  - Yes, sometimes
  - No
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- Does the person ever need someone to help with, or be with them for, communication activities?
  - Yes, always
  - Yes, sometimes
  - No

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- What are the reasons for the need for assistance or supervision? (Select all that apply)
  - No need for assistance
  - Short-term health condition (lasting less than six months)
  - Long-term health condition (lasting six months or more)
  - Disability (lasting six months or more)
  - Old or young age
  - Difficulty with English language
  - Other reason

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

`r note_caveat_underidentification`

`r note_caveat_unknown_agesex`

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- People requiring assistance with core activities were defined as those needing assistance in their day to day lives in one or more of the three core activity areas of self-care, mobility, and communication because of:
  - a long-term health condition (lasting six months or more),
  - a disability (lasting six months or more), or
  - old age.

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::
